af95fd.risk_area: Path traversal via S3 object keys
af95fd.evidence: Filed as vuln-0025-family path traversal report vuln-0027 (medium, confidence medium). workspace-sync.ts:77-85/94: relativePath = key.slice(prefix.length) joined to WORKSPACE_DIR with no containment check; local PoC (mocked S3, real fs) shows ../../ escapes WORKSPACE_DIR. Prerequisite: attacker-controlled S3 keys in the workspace prefix (no tenant-reachable write primitive found; shared/compromised bucket scenario). Report also covers sibling resolveWorkspaceFilePath startsWith-without-separator bypass (workspace-manager.ts:1554-1555, verified) and unvalidated filePath in readWorkspaceFileFromS3 (:1495-1530).

history.evidence: Line ~78: `path.join(WORKSPACE_DIR, relativePath)` where relativePath = key.slice(prefix.length) with no containment check. Node path.join locally confirmed `s3://bucket/pfx/../../etc/cron.d/pwn` → `/etc/cron.d/pwn`, escaping /workspace. The container runs as non-root but /app is chown node:node (Dockerfile), so overwriting /app/node_modules = code exec on next invocation. Attacker prerequisite: ability to write objects with `../` keys into the shared workspace bucket (execution role has bucket-wide s3:PutObject per infra/scripts/agentcore-permissions.json). Whether AgentCore containers are reused across tenants/invocations is unverifiable locally — static trace only.

CONFIRMED via local unit PoC (agentcore vitest, real path.join/fs): key `ws/../../tmp/rce-poc/sync-escaped.txt` under prefix `ws/` → workspace-sync.ts:78-79 `relativePath = key.slice(prefix.length)` then `path.join(WORKSPACE_DIR, relativePath)` resolves to `/tmp/rce-poc/sync-escaped.txt` — outside WORKSPACE_DIR (/workspace); mkdirSync/createWriteStream follow. Observed: localPath printed `/tmp/rce-poc/sync-escaped.txt`, no containment check anywhere in the restore loop. Prerequisite: attacker must control an S3 object key under the workspace prefix (workflow workspace upload path is backend-controlled; exploitation requires write access to that bucket/prefix or MITM of S3 traffic). Reachability from a tenant user is indirect — the bucket key layout is server-generated, so this is a malicious/compromised-S3-content or shared-bucket issue, not direct tenant input.

784c32.evidence: Filed as sibling weakness in vuln-0027 (path containment family). readWorkspaceFileFromS3 / readWorkspaceFileFromS3Raw (workspace-manager.ts:1495-1530) build `key = ${orgId}/${scopeId}/${sessionId}/${filePath}` with completely unvalidated filePath — ../ segments or leading / target keys outside the session prefix. history.evidence: Local FS read path (readWorkspaceFile:1467) enforces resolved.startsWith(workspacePath), but the S3 fallback builds key = `${orgId}/${scopeId}/${sessionId}/${filePath}` with unvalidated filePath — a query path like ../../../<otherOrg>/... escapes the session prefix (S3 has no path semantics, prefix not enforced server-side). Session itself is org-checked via chatService.getSessionById, but filePath flows straight into the key. Note org/scope/session IDs are UUIDs, so traversal targets must be guessable keys; severity constrained by key guessability.

Assessed (static + local key-construction test): readWorkspaceFileFromS3 (workspace-manager.ts:1495-1530) and readWorkspaceFileFromS3Raw build `key = ${orgId}/${scopeId}/${sessionId}/${filePath}` with completely unvalidated filePath (query param at chat.routes.ts:1094/1220, execution.routes.ts:626) — `../../../<otherOrg>/...` yields a key outside the session prefix, and unlike the local-FS path there is NO startsWith check at all on the S3 path. Containment on S3 keys is absent, not merely prefix-weak. Reachability constraints: caller must already be an authenticated org member with access to the chat session/execution (session ownership is org-scoped per separate finding), and target file must exist in the bucket under a guessable key path; S3 does not normalize `..` so traversal only works to keys literally containing dot-dot segments that were uploaded that way — the backend's own uploads use clean generated keys. Practical impact: mainly a same-bucket arbitrary-key read if other tenants' data is stored with attacker-derivable prefixes. Real but constrained; UUID-guessability limits blind targeting.

9a1e13.surface: frontend token-in-URL: Chat.tsx:617-634/645, ProjectBoard.tsx:190-197, WorkspaceActions.tsx:179-184, Chat.tsx:296-304 (pdfUrl) + backend auth.ts:150 accepting ?token=
9a1e13.risk_area: JWT leakage via query string (browser history, Referer, logs)
9a1e13.evidence: Frontend appends full JWT (local_auth_token or cognito_id_token) as ?token= query param when building iframe/src and window.open URLs for published apps, dev-server previews, PDFs and raw file downloads. Backend middleware/auth.ts:150-157 explicitly accepts query token ('or ?token query param for iframe/img src'). Tokens end up in browser history, server/proxy access logs, and Referer headers of any subresources the preview pages load. No HttpOnly cookie alternative exists. Attacker prerequisites: access to logs/history or Referer leak from preview content. Validated by code trace both sides.

9ba188.surface: frontend browser storage: services/cognito.ts (TOKEN_KEYS localStorage incl. refresh_token), services/auth.ts:50-62, services/api/restClient.ts:26-32,46-58
9ba188.risk_area: token storage in localStorage / session handling
9ba188.evidence: All tokens (local JWT, Cognito id/access/refresh tokens) are stored in localStorage, not sessionStorage or HttpOnly cookies — XSS-stealable and the refresh token persists indefinitely (no clearTokens on getIdToken expiry, only on failed refresh). Logout is reasonably complete: AuthContext.logout → cognito logout() clears all 5 keys and redirects to Cognito logout; localLogout clears local token. restClient.setAuthToken also writes 'cognito_id_token' key, mixing modes. This is a hardening/defense-in-depth finding (storage choice amplifies any future XSS; no demonstrated XSS exists — all render paths are escaped). Not a standalone vulnerability.

2f3f56.surface: frontend sandboxed iframes: Chat.tsx:596-600 & 642-647 & AppRunner.tsx:160 (sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups"), Chat.tsx:122-127 srcDoc iframe
2f3f56.evidence: Resolved by vuln-0003 (filed by Frontend Reporting Agent) covering Chat.tsx:600,646 and AppRunner.tsx:160 sandbox policy; code-trace validated with topology precondition documented.

history.evidence: allow-scripts + allow-same-origin together defeat the sandbox when the framed document is same-origin with a privileged origin. The preview URLs point at the backend origin (VITE_API_BASE_URL), so allow-same-origin grants framed content full access to the BACKEND origin (where the ?token= URLs also live), not the frontend origin — sandbox removal capability exists but direct impact is limited since backend origin holds no DOM/storage secrets the frontend relies on. HtmlPreview srcDoc (Chat.tsx:122-127) uses allow-scripts WITHOUT allow-same-origin → opaque origin, scripts run isolated — acceptable for an HTML preview feature of agent output. Recommend dropping allow-same-origin; needs deployment topology confirmation (whether API and SPA share an origin in prod) to rate severity.

b9fc54.surface: frontend route gating: ProtectedRoute.tsx (auth-only), Dashboard.tsx:115 / Settings.tsx:36 isAdmin client checks, no role-based route guards in App.tsx
b9fc54.evidence: Backend spot-checks found matching server-side enforcement on admin-sensitive surfaces: organizations.routes.ts uses requireRole('owner'/'admin') on all mutating routes; audit.routes.ts requires requireAdminAccess; apiKeys list is scoped to request.user.orgId (own-org keys only, keyed prefixes not secrets); support/execution/tasks routes all carry authenticate (+requireModifyAccess for writes). Client-side isAdmin checks are cosmetic (UI visibility), no missing-backend-guard pair found in sampled routes. Frontend client is generic — an authenticated member calling admin APIs directly is rejected server-side. Residual risk: 45 route files, ~6 sampled + WS gateway (covered separately) — a full per-route audit was out of my scope.

55972b.surface: frontend secrets exposure: .env.example, src/**, public/**, vite.config.ts, dcv-sdk bundle
55972b.risk_area: hardcoded API keys / Supabase keys / secrets in frontend source
55972b.evidence: .env.example contains only placeholders (your-anon-key-here). No createClient/supabase usage found in src despite @supabase/supabase-js dependency (unused dependency — dead weight, no exposure). No hardcoded keys, tokens or secrets in src/ or public/ (public contains only the vendored NICE DCV SDK bundle and assets). Cognito config comes from backend /api/auth/config or VITE_ env at build time.

5cf7a3.surface: frontend SSE/chatStreamService.ts (fetch POST /api/chat/stream with Authorization header), SessionStreamManager.ts:294
5cf7a3.risk_area: stream endpoint auth and URL construction
5cf7a3.evidence: SSE clients use authenticated fetch (Bearer header via getAuthToken) against fixed VITE_API_BASE_URL endpoints — no user-influenced URL, no WebSocket, no query-token. Origin validation N/A for fetch-based SSE.

4491cb.surface: frontend react-markdown renderers: TextContentBlock.tsx:62-134, Chat.tsx:115 MarkdownPreview, ChatRoom.tsx:553, ProjectBoard.tsx:760, WorkflowCopilot.tsx
4491cb.risk_area: markdown rendering of agent output (raw HTML, link safety)
4491cb.evidence: All ReactMarkdown usages are default-escaping (no rehype-raw, no skipHtml, no urlTransform override — raw HTML in markdown is rendered as inert text). Custom link renderer in TextContentBlock.tsx:104-107 uses target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer". Markdown in Chat/ChatRoom/ProjectBoard/WorkflowCopilot has no custom anchor override but react-markdown default urlTransform sanitizes javascript: URLs. javascript: href risk via default renderer: react-markdown's defaultUrlTransform only allows http/https/mailto etc. — safe.

6898fd.surface: backend CORS config (app.ts:79-100, config/index.ts:64 CORS_ORIGIN default '*')
6898fd.risk_area: CORS wildcard + credentials:true with Bearer-token auth model
6898fd.evidence: Confirmed default is origin:true (reflect any origin) + credentials:true when CORS_ORIGIN='*'. However the backend uses no cookies anywhere (auth is Authorization: Bearer JWT; no setCookie in middleware/auth.ts; only logging redaction mentions cookie) — credentialed cross-origin reads therefore cannot attach ambient credentials, and the API requires an explicit Bearer token an attacker's page never possesses. gen-base-env.py does not set CORS_ORIGIN, so the wildcard default ships in deployment, but with token-header auth the impact is limited to unauthenticated/public endpoints (webhook trigger, avatar generate, Swagger) which are same-data regardless of origin. Weak misconfig observation, already folded into the config finding (entry ea19f7); not an independent exploitable vuln.

799b31.surface: chat.service.ts:126 getSessionById + chat.routes.ts session detail/workspace endpoints
799b31.risk_area: horizontal IDOR within org (session sharing design intent)
799b31.evidence: Session detail endpoints (getSessionById) are org-scoped but not user-scoped, and the session LIST endpoint is user-scoped (getSessions → findByUser, chat.service.ts:105-106) — so other users' sessions never appear in a member's UI list; cross-user access is only possible by guessing/enumerating session UUIDs. No code comment documents org-level sharing as intended, but the related KB/file scoping precedent in this codebase is org-level (file.service.ts org-prefix checks), and the Backend AuthZ Agent already filed this org-level scoping family (chat IDOR entry a8217e / vuln reports). No separate exploitable finding beyond what's already reported; reclassify as already-covered design observation rather than a distinct vuln.

a02b90.risk_area: backend API key persistence across AgentCore container invocations
a02b90.evidence: agentcore is a long-lived node http server (src/index.ts:27+): each POST /invocations writes payload.backend_api_key into process.env.AUTH_TOKEN and it is never cleared after the invocation's SSE stream ends. If the AgentCore runtime reuses one container across invocations (its documented execution model), the key from invocation N stays in the env for invocation N+1 — potentially a different tenant's invocation, where workspace files from prior runs could also persist (same code never cleans /workspace between invocations either; restoreWorkspaceFromS3 overwrites but doesn't clear). Cannot determine from the local repo whether AgentCore containers are reused per-tenant or torn down per invocation (platform lifecycle outside this codebase) — open proof gap; even if reused, the values are per-org backend keys within the same deployment, limiting cross-tenant impact. Not reportable without container lifecycle evidence.

22400a.evidence: Verified: @fastify/swagger-ui registered at routePrefix '/docs' with no preHandler/auth and no env gate — the full OpenAPI spec (all endpoint schemas) is reachable unauthenticated. This is reconnaissance/information disclosure only (no secrets in the spec; schemas describe the API). Standard low/info observation; folded into existing config/misconfig findings rather than a standalone vuln report.
